## Tena: a city at the gateway to Ecuador's Amazon

Tena lies on the eastern slopes of the Andes in Napo Province. It is the starting point for river trips and journeys into forested areas that differ markedly from the high-altitude routes around [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). You can stay in the city before an active rafting trip, an excursion to waterfalls, or several days in the Amazon region.

Ecuador's national tourism portal describes Tena as a destination for nature, rafting, kayaking, hiking, encounters with local communities, and gastronomy. To make the most of a visit, decide in advance what matters most: river sports, a gentle rainforest walk, or a cultural program.

## Rafting and river routes

One of the area's best-known active routes follows the [Jatunyacu River](/ecuador/place/jatunyacu-river/). Rafting takes place here, with difficulty depending on the stretch of river, season, and water level. Gentler sections are suitable for some groups, while others involve technically demanding whitewater under the supervision of experienced instructors.

Kayaking and rafting are different activities. A rafting group shares an inflatable raft; kayaking requires separate boat-handling skills. Even if a regional description mentions both, a specific tour may include only one of them.

The safety considerations are practical: qualified instructors, helmets, life jackets, acceptable levels of exertion, and weather conditions. Heavy rain can change water levels and the riverbed's characteristics, so operators adapt outings to the actual conditions.

## Waterfalls, forest trails, and nature areas

There are waterfalls and small natural areas around Tena that visitors reach by car and then on foot. Ecuador's official tourism portal mentions Latas and Alto Pusuno waterfalls, as well as walking routes near Talag.

Nearby forest trails focus on plants, birds, and the characteristics of humid tropical ecosystems. Unlike the Andean high-altitude reserves, this region is warm and humid; paths can be slippery, and reaching the trailhead may take a significant part of the day.

If wildlife observation is your main goal, the duration of a walk and the experience of a local guide often matter more than a list of sites. A forest walk does not guarantee sightings of monkeys, toucans, or other particular species.

## Kichwa culture and the cuisine of Napo Province

Kichwa communities live around Tena and maintain traditions connected to rivers, forests, crafts, and local food. A community visit should follow an agreed program: simply staying in town does not include participating in ceremonies, entering private homes, or photographing people without permission.

One characteristic regional dish is *maito*: fish or meat cooked in leaves and served with local side dishes. Yuca and other Amazonian ingredients feature in local cuisine. You can discover these dishes in a local restaurant; watching their preparation requires a separate arrangement.

## Getting to Tena

Tena is reached by road from Quito across the eastern Andes. The journey passes through several altitude zones, so weather en route may differ considerably from conditions in town. The [Papallacta hot springs](/ecuador/place/papallacta/) lie along the way and can be planned as a separate stop.

| What to plan | What to check |
|---|---|
| Drive from Quito | Mountain weather and traffic |
| Rafting | River difficulty and instructors |
| Forest excursion | Travel and walking time |
| Community visit | Program and prior arrangements |

Tena works for both a short visit and several days of river activities. More remote Amazon lodges along the [Napo River](/ecuador/place/napo-river/), however, can be much farther away and require their own transfer arrangements.

## Tena on Ada Tours itineraries

On the [Active Ecuador tour](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/), Tena is associated with rafting on the Jatunyacu and a subsequent visit to Papallacta's hot springs. This day requires organization for a sporting activity and suits travelers interested in being active on the water.

Our [11-day journey through the Andes, Amazon, and Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/) has a different Amazon section, focused on the river area and accommodation at a lodge. It should not automatically be equated with rafting in Tena: each route must be assessed by its own itinerary.

For comparison, see our [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and [adventure travel](/interests/adventure/).

## Frequently asked questions about Tena

### Where is Tena located?

In Napo Province, east of the Andes in Ecuador's Amazon region. It is the provincial capital and a starting point for trips to nearby rivers and forests.

### Can I go rafting near Tena?

Yes. One well-known rafting route follows the Jatunyacu River. Operators choose a suitable section based on group experience and water levels.

### How does Tena differ from Coca?

Tena is linked to road routes, forest walks, and river activities in Napo Province. [Coca](/ecuador/place/coca/) is often used for onward river transfers to remote Amazon lodges. They are different transport hubs.

### Can Tena be combined with Papallacta?

Yes. [Papallacta](/ecuador/place/papallacta/) lies on the eastern road from Quito and can be a stop on the way to the Amazon region.

## Choosing a tour through Tena in the Ecuadorian Amazon

[Tena](/ecuador/place/tena/) lies in Napo Province in eastern Ecuador. Roads from the Andes pass through the area toward Amazonian rivers, forest trails, and river lodges. It is an opportunity to add a completely different environment to the highland volcanoes and cities: humid tropical forest and river activities.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Tena on the main route. **A mention of the town does not mean rafting, walks around Tena, or an overnight stay in its center are included.** In our itineraries, it serves different roles: a base for rafting or a waypoint on the road to a canoe landing.

## Which itineraries go through Tena?

### Nine active days in Ecuador, including rafting

The [Active Ecuador tour](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/) combines highland regions with a full rafting day. The route includes volcano walks, [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/), canyoning, and **rafting on the [Jatunyacu River](/ecuador/place/jatunyacu-river/)** near Tena. The river is also known as the Upper Napo; the rafting route alternates rapids with calmer stretches. Previous rafting experience is not required for this trip. Lunch and a return to the hotel follow the rafting activity.

Next, travelers visit the hot springs at [Papallacta](/ecuador/place/papallacta/) before returning to Quito. This is a mainland itinerary, **without a separate Galápagos section**. It suits travelers who want several types of active recreation in one trip and are ready to assess each day's physical demands.

### Eleven days via Tena to the Napo River and Galápagos

On the [Ecuador: Andes, Amazon and Galápagos itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/), the road from Baños leads toward Tena and then [Punta Ahuano](/ecuador/place/punta-ahuano/). There, you transfer to a canoe and travel downstream along the [Napo River](/ecuador/place/napo-river/) to Casa del Suizo Lodge. The Amazon section lasts **3 days / 2 nights**, and the activities at the lodge are selected with a local guide. A list of possible activities does not mean all of them are included every day.

After the Amazon, the route goes through Papallacta and then continues to the Galápagos Islands. Here Tena links the road transfer with the boat journey. **Rafting from the active nine-day itinerary cannot automatically be added to this program**: it has different confirmed arrangements and a different purpose for its Amazon section.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_aktivnyj_ekvador,tour_source_ves_ekvador_galapagosskie_ostrova}}

| Program | Main focus |
|---|---|
| [Active Ecuador](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/) | Rafting on the Jatunyacu |
| [Andes, Amazon and Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/) | Napo River lodge followed by the islands |

## Why transfers between the Andes and Amazon matter

There is a noticeable change in climate between [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) and Tena: cool highland valleys give way to warm, humid river landscapes. On the short trip, the rafting day calls for particular preparation; on the lodge itinerary, the drive is followed by canoe boarding and transport of belongings by water. Different formats require different luggage arrangements and travel-time allowances.

Rafting calls for appropriate clothing, a life jacket, a briefing, and following the guide's instructions. For a lodge transfer, lightweight quick-drying clothes and waterproof protection for documents and electronics are more practical. Rain can change river conditions. Ask about the specific difficulty of the rafting route and boarding arrangements rather than relying only on a general description of the Amazon.

If your priority is **sport and physical activity**, compare [Ecuador adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/ecuador/). If forests, rivers, and natural landscapes matter more, see the [Nature tour selection](/interests/nature/tours/ecuador/). Both catalogs contain different itineraries; not all go directly through Tena.

## What to check before booking

Compare the number of nights in the Amazon region, accommodation, transfers to the lodge, included excursions, guide language, and onward flights. On the nine-day trip, Tena is linked to rafting; on the eleven-day trip, it is part of the road to Punta Ahuano and a riverside lodge. Even though both journeys cross eastern Ecuador, **they are not interchangeable**.

Rain is possible in the Amazon during different seasons, and conditions on the water and forest trails change. A forecast for Quito does not describe weather around the Napo. Bring protection against rain, sun, and insects, and discuss your readiness for sporting activities before booking.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Tena

### Is rafting included on every tour through Tena?

No. [Rafting on the Jatunyacu](/ecuador/place/jatunyacu-river/) is part of the [nine-day active tour](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/). The eleven-day program via Tena confirms the journey to Punta Ahuano and the Napo lodge, but does not list rafting as an included service.

### Can I visit Tena without flying to the Galápagos?

Yes. The [Active Ecuador tour](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/) takes place on the mainland and ends with a return to Quito.

### Do all programs include an overnight stay in Tena itself?

There is no basis for that claim. The second itinerary names Casa del Suizo Lodge after the transfer to Punta Ahuano. Check the precise accommodation locations in the individual program, not just a list of towns.

### Do I need rafting experience for the active tour?

The [active itinerary](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/) does not require previous experience. However, participation entails a safety briefing and depends on river conditions and individual restrictions. Agree on the detailed rafting arrangements before traveling.

## Tigua in Ecuador: painting in highland villages

Tigua is an area of settlements in Cotopaxi Province known for the work of Kichwa artists. Their paintings are recognizable by their vivid colors and detailed depictions of mountains, fields, animals, village festivities, and everyday Andean life. Visiting Tigua is especially rewarding because the art tells the community's stories in its own visual language.

The Smithsonian's National Museum of the American Indian holds paintings by artists from Tigua, including works by Alfredo, Gustavo, and Magdalena Toaquiza Ugsha. Museum records identify the artists, their *Tigua Kichua* cultural affiliation, and materials such as sheepskin and acrylic or oil paints. This confirms an established artistic tradition, not simply a souvenir style created for tourists.

## Why paint on sheepskin?

Painted animal hide is one of the characteristic materials of Tigua art. Traditionally the hide was stretched on a wooden frame; today techniques and materials can vary between workshops. When buying a piece, ask the artist what the particular work is painted on: original paintings on sheepskin, canvas, or other materials should not all be described in the same way.

The compositions often tell a whole story on one surface. Mountain pastures, people in traditional dress, animals, rural houses, dances, and celebrations appear side by side. Such scenes are fascinating not only for their colors but also for the arrangement of figures and the ways the artists depict local life.

The best introduction is to look at several paintings by different artists. Pay attention to individual technique, signatures, materials, and provenance. Buying directly from an artist can support local craftsmanship, but confirm the terms of purchase and shipping on site.

## Arranging a workshop visit

Tigua is easy to combine with a journey through Ecuador's highlands, particularly if the route continues to [Quilotoa Lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/). A studio stop differs from a conventional museum: visitors may discuss the subjects of the art, see tools and finished pieces, and, when possible, learn about how the paintings are made.

Meeting a particular artist or attending a demonstration depends on prior arrangements. Simply stopping at Tigua does not guarantee that every painter will be present, that an original piece will be available to purchase, or that a class will take place. Arrange such details as part of the itinerary.

Mountain roads and changing weather mean that transfers need sufficient time. If Tigua lies between [Quito and Cotopaxi Volcano](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) and Quilotoa, leave time both for the paintings and for viewpoints over the crater lake, rather than reducing the visit to a quick stop before driving onward.

## What Tigua paintings reveal about the Andes

These paintings show Cotopaxi through the eyes of local residents. Agriculture, animals, mountain fields, festive processions, and crafts appear not as random "ethnic motifs" but as episodes from the life of a particular community.

For travelers in Ecuador, this is a valuable complement to volcanoes and panoramic landscapes. [Quilotoa](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) introduces the region's natural history, while Tigua introduces the people living in these highlands and creating its contemporary culture. For more cultural experiences, see [history and traditions journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/) and [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/).

## Practical advice

Bring an extra warm layer and sun protection for a walk through a mountain settlement: weather and perceived temperatures can change rapidly at altitude. Reaching nearby attractions takes time, so account for road conditions and stops when planning.

Treat artists' workshops as their working spaces. Ask permission before photographing people or works of art. If you would like to buy a painting, check its dimensions, material, packing, and payment options.

## Frequently asked questions about Tigua

### What is Tigua famous for?

The vivid paintings of Kichwa artists depicting the life of Andean communities. The Smithsonian collection includes works by Tigua painters on sheepskin.

### Can I buy a painting from a local artist?

Works are sold in workshops, but the availability of particular artists and paintings varies by day and arrangement. Ask the creator directly about the provenance of the piece you choose.

### What is convenient to visit together with Tigua?

[Quilotoa crater lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) is in the same highland part of Ecuador. Combining art and natural scenery makes for a more varied journey.

### Is Tigua a separate painting technique?

It is primarily an artistic tradition and a community of painters. Sheepskin is a characteristic support for many paintings, but materials and personal styles vary.

## Choosing a tour through Tigua in Ecuador

[Tigua](/ecuador/place/tigua/) is a highland settlement in Cotopaxi Province known for folk painting. Local artists depict volcanoes, rural scenery, animals, and episodes of Andean community life. A visit to a workshop is often combined with a journey to [Quilotoa Lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/): in one day, travelers encounter both local craftsmanship and the nature of the central Andes.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Tigua on the main route. **A visit to Tigua does not make this a multi-day art-focused tour.** On these programs, Tigua is primarily a stop on the way to Quilotoa. Choose by the regions visited before and after that stop.

## A short route through Tigua: five days on the mainland

The [five-day private mainland Ecuador tour](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-private-tour-5-days/) combines Quito, the [Mindo](/ecuador/place/mindo/) cloud forests, a craft workshop in Tigua, and the road to Quilotoa. It offers an introduction to contrasting mainland landscapes in a limited time, **without an island extension**.

Day 4 includes a workshop visit where you can see traditional paintings of Andean landscapes on hide. The route then continues toward the crater lake. If Tigua is one of several cultural stops among natural attractions for you, this short program is designed for precisely that purpose.

## Tigua on journeys that include the Galápagos Islands

On the [eight-day Complete Ecuador and Galápagos Islands tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-galapagos-islands/), a Tigua stop precedes the visit to Quilotoa, while subsequent days focus on the archipelago. [Another eight-day itinerary through Quito, Quilotoa, and Mindo](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-quito-quilotoa-mindo-july/) also goes through the village before continuing to the Galápagos. Compare these trips by their precise island programs, not simply their total duration.

The [11-day Best of Ecuador: Guaranteed Departures tour](/ecuador/tour/best-of-ecuador-guaranteed-departures/) continues its mainland section after Tigua and Quilotoa through [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/), Riobamba, the [Chimborazo](/ecuador/place/chimborazo-reserve/) area, Ingapirca, and Cuenca. Only then do travelers head to the Galápagos. Choose this itinerary to visit more regions of the country.

On the [Complete Ecuador New Year program](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/), Tigua is scheduled for January 1, 2027, while the full trip runs from December 30, 2026 to January 9, 2027. The cultural stop is part of a route through the Andes and Galápagos. These dates belong to that specific tour, not to a general schedule for visits to Tigua.

## Longer journeys: the Amazon and an island cruise

The [15-day Ecuador and Amazon highlights journey](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-amazon-15-days/) combines Tigua and Quilotoa with a separate Amazon stage. It suits travelers who want to devote more time to mainland nature areas and return to Quito without a mandatory flight to the Galápagos.

The [18-day Ecuador journey with a Galápagos cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) includes Tigua en route to Quilotoa near the end of the mainland section, followed by travel around the islands. Here it is useful to assess the major trip stages, flight durations, and cruise conditions. One studio visit does not define such a long itinerary.

| Route | Key difference |
|---|---|
| [5 days on the mainland](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-private-tour-5-days/) | Quito, Mindo, Tigua, Quilotoa |
| [8 days with islands](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-galapagos-islands/) | Short combination of mainland and sea |
| [15 days with Amazon](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-amazon-15-days/) | Mainland nature areas |
| [18 days with a cruise](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-wildlife-cruise-18-days/) | Several regions and an expedition |

There is also an [Ecuador, Galápagos, and Humpback Whales tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/) that passes through Tigua. For this journey, check the actual season and dates of the marine section rather than expecting whale watching during the highland village visit.

## What to see at Tigua on your journey

Local paintings are famous for bright colors and scenes from everyday Andean life. Workshops offer a chance to discover artists' works, traditional materials, and depictions of volcanoes, animals, festivities, and village scenes. Our itineraries visit such workshops on the way to Quilotoa.

**A visit to a workshop is not the same as a paid, private painting lesson.** If you would like a practical class with an artist, an extended visit to several workshops, or a meeting with a particular painter, arrangements and conditions must be agreed separately. Tigua's inclusion in the itinerary does not promise these experiences.

At nearby [Quilotoa](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/), the natural portion of the day features a volcanic crater, viewpoints, and potential walks down toward the water. Tigua and Quilotoa are therefore best understood as **two distinct stops on one mountain day**. For a wider cultural comparison, see the [Ecuador Culture and History tour catalog](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/ecuador/).

## Preparing for this day in the central Andes

A workshop visit does not require much exertion, but the road to the lake passes through high-altitude terrain. Some programs offer a descent to the crater lake, the ascent back up, kayaking, or other activities. These may have special conditions or incur additional charges; do not assume they are included on every tour.

Bring comfortable shoes, clothes suitable for wind and rain, water, and sun protection. If traveling soon after arriving in Quito, allow for acclimatization to altitude and assess your readiness for physical exertion individually.

Your onward route after Tigua also affects the pace: returning to Quito, heading toward Baños, continuing through [Chimborazo Reserve](/ecuador/place/chimborazo-reserve/), or flying onward to the [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) require different amounts of time. Browse all combinations in the [Ecuador tour catalog](/ecuador/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Tigua

### Do all tours through Tigua include a painting workshop class?

No. Several itineraries mention visiting a craft studio and learning about local painting. A complete lesson with an artist is not confirmed as a separate service and should not be assumed included.

### Can I visit Tigua without going to the Galápagos?

Yes. The [five-day mainland route](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-private-tour-5-days/) and the [15-day Amazon program](/ecuador/tour/mainland-ecuador-amazon-15-days/) include Tigua without a mandatory Galápagos stage.

### Are Tigua and Quilotoa the same place?

No. [Tigua](/ecuador/place/tigua/) is a settlement and center of folk painting; [Quilotoa](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) is a crater lake. Many itineraries visit both in one day, but the stops are different.

### How long does a visit to Tigua take?

On existing combination routes, it is generally a stop on the way to Quilotoa. For a longer encounter with local artists, the time and content must be arranged separately; they cannot be inferred from the overall tour duration.

## Tintoreras in the Galápagos: lava islets and reef sharks

Tintoreras is a group of small volcanic islets off the southern shore of [Isabela Island](/ecuador/place/isabela-island/) in Ecuador's Galápagos archipelago. Their defining features are black lava formations, narrow channels of clear water, and the remarkable proximity of marine wildlife. The excursion suits travelers who want to experience island nature from a boat and on a short walk along an approved route.

The name Tintoreras is associated with sharks found in the channels between the lava shores. These are whitetip reef sharks, *Triaenodon obesus*. During the day, they often rest in sheltered underwater spots, making it possible to see them from shore without entering the water. Sightings depend on conditions and animal behavior; no one can guarantee sharks will be present in every channel.

## Where the islets are and how excursions work

The closest base for visiting Tintoreras is [Puerto Villamil](/ecuador/place/puerto-villamil/) on Isabela. According to the Galápagos National Park administration, the boat journey from the town takes roughly 10 minutes. This short crossing brings visitors to the shores and wildlife of a protected site.

| Stage | What you may see |
|---|---|
| Boat trip | Lava shores and coves |
| Walk | Volcanic rocks and iguanas |
| Channels | Possible shark sightings |

This is an outline of a typical visit to the islets, not a set of services guaranteed on every excursion. Exact stops, duration, and sequence depend on the program, sea conditions, and permitted sections of the national park.

Tintoreras often forms part of a busy sightseeing day on Isabela. If you are traveling from another island in the archipelago, a much longer inter-island boat crossing or a flight must be added to the short trip from Puerto Villamil. The overall travel time therefore cannot be estimated from the distance between the town and the islets alone.

## Wildlife at Tintoreras

### Whitetip reef sharks

The narrow lava channels are Tintoreras' most recognizable natural feature. Small reef sharks known in Spanish as *tintoreras* may rest there. Visitors can observe them through clear water from a safe distance. Do not interfere with their behavior, feed them, or move closer simply for a photograph.

### Marine iguanas

Marine iguanas are endemic to the Galápagos Islands. They often rest on dark lava, warm themselves in the sun, and enter the sea to feed. At Tintoreras, watching where you step and following guides' instructions are especially important: parts of the lava may serve as nesting grounds.

The national park has reported temporary closures of some trail sections to protect marine iguana clutches. This is a conservation measure, not evidence that the entire excursion is permanently inaccessible. When part of a route is closed, visitors must use an approved alternative.

### Sea lions, turtles, and birds

Sea lions and sea turtles inhabit the waters around Isabela; with luck, you may see them during the boat crossing. On shore, birds and small habitats formed by lava flows are worth noticing. Wildlife observations differ each day: animals move freely and may be away from the usual route.

## Tintoreras, Concha de Perla, and Sierra Negra Volcano

Several popular natural attractions on Isabela are sometimes blended into one description even though their programs are very different. Tintoreras is mainly a group of lava islets visited for walks and coastal wildlife. Concha de Perla is a sheltered bay often chosen for exploring underwater life. [Sierra Negra Volcano](/ecuador/place/sierra-negra-volcano/) is in Isabela's highlands and requires a completely different land-based excursion.

If you hope to see sharks in lava channels and marine iguanas, Tintoreras is the appropriate choice. For snorkeling, check separately which site and equipment are part of the specific day: swimming and other underwater activities cannot automatically be attributed to every tour mentioning the islets.

## National park rules

The Galápagos is a protected natural archipelago with regulated routes. Follow your authorized guide, stay on the marked trail, and keep your distance from wildlife. Even when a marine iguana lies motionless, do not approach it for photos.

The national park administration may restrict access to particular areas because of nesting, habitat restoration, landing conditions, or other conservation measures. The operator should therefore confirm the current route on the day of the excursion. Extending a walk by leaving the permitted trail is prohibited.

Wear enclosed nonslip shoes and sun protection on lava paths. Surfaces can be uneven and sharp. Protect belongings from spray on the boat and follow the captain's instructions in rough seas.

## When to plan a visit

In the Galápagos, actual water conditions and wind matter as much as the month. Navigation conditions and the distribution of marine wildlife vary by season. Try to schedule the excursion on a day that allows some flexibility, particularly if it is combined with an inter-island transfer.

Tintoreras should not be treated as a full beach day. The main activity is observing the wildlife of protected volcanic islets. For a longer rest or underwater activities on Isabela, choose other sites and appropriate arrangements.

## Tintoreras on Ada Tours itineraries

On our [14-day journey through Ecuador and the Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-nature-discovery/), you visit Tintoreras during a day on Isabela. First you explore the island's natural areas; after lunch, you travel to the volcanic islets, where sea lions, turtles, iguanas, and sharks may be seen. Actual wildlife sightings depend on nature, not on a timetable.

Tintoreras is also listed on our [Quito–Galápagos Islands itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-quito-galapagos-islands/). When comparing these trips, check how much time is allocated to Isabela, where overnight stays take place, and whether the excursion to the islets itself is included. You can also browse [all Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) and [wildlife-watching journeys](/interests/wildlife/).

## Frequently asked questions about Tintoreras

### Where are the Tintoreras Islets?

Near Puerto Villamil, off Isabela Island in Ecuador's Galápagos archipelago. Boats usually depart from the town for the islets.

### Can sharks be seen without diving?

Sometimes, yes. Whitetip reef sharks rest in lava channels and may be visible from a permitted section of the trail. Their presence and visibility cannot be guaranteed.

### Can I visit Tintoreras independently?

This is protected national park territory. Visits follow authorized routes and current rules with appropriate guides. Visitors cannot freely walk onto any stretch of lava shore.

### Are Tintoreras and Concha de Perla the same place?

No. They are different natural sites near Puerto Villamil. Tintoreras is known for its lava channels and iguanas; Concha de Perla is primarily visited for its sheltered bay and underwater wildlife.
